newsitem.title: USA: Olympic Financial shares rise on accounting plan.
newsitem.headline: Olympic Financial shares rise on accounting plan.

text.p: Olympic Financial Ltd shares rose more than 16 percent after the auto finance company outlined a more conservative procedure for accounting for the losses it can recover by selling repossessed autos.
"I think that they made a convincing argument that they were changing their way of doing business and we're being more conservative," Robert Ollech, analyst at Principal Financial Securities, said.
Olympic stock was up 1-3/8 at 9-1/8 Thursday and was the biggest percent gainer on the New York Stock Exchange.
Olympic Thursday said it increased its loan loss reserves to reflect the assumed reductions in the amount of a loan that can be recovered on a repossessed vehicle.
Olympic also said it expects net income from operations for the 12-months ending March 31, 1998, to be at least $1.

"That looks like a pretty fair number right now," Ollech said. He noted the Minneapolis-based company appears to be getting delinquencies under control and using more loan officers. Loans delinquent over 30 days were 2.34 percent in the first quarter versus 2.64 percent in the fourth quarter.
But some concern remains about the company's move into what it calls the "classic" credit area, which are loans to people without perfect credit, but whose credit is better than sub-prime.
Standard and Poor's Thursday cut its outlook on Olympic to negative from stable.

"Although the announced accounting changes and policies are pruddent and bring the company more in line with practices of industry peers, Standard & Poor's still remains concerned about the company's rapid growth of higher-risk "classic" auto lending program, and the resulting increases in delinquencies and loan losses," the rating agency said in a news release.
